material_definitions: The substitution of P5+ with Si4+ was performed in the solid solutions Li6+xP1-xSixS5X to increase the Li+ concentration.
Aliovalent doping in superionic compounds like argyrodites is used to increase the number of charge carriers and ionic conductivity.
Thiophosphates exhibit high conductivities and low activation barriers due to the polarizable PS4 3- anion.
The argyrodites Li6PS5X exhibit a site disorder between halide and sulfide ions that influences ionic transport.
The available Li+ positions form cage-like local polyhedra for ion jumps that can be divided into three possible jump processes.
warnings: Temperature not explicitly stated in the provided text snippet; assumed room temperature (25 °C).
Conductivity value reported as 'greater than 2 mS cm-1'.

material_definitions: The study explores the Li6+xP1-xSixS5Br solid solution series, where Si4+ is substituted for P5+ to increase lithium content.
Ionic conductivity was evaluated using temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy on pellet samples.
Samples were fit with an equivalent circuit consisting of a parallel constant phase element (CPE) and resistor in series with a blocking electrode CPE.
Scanning electron microscopy confirmed high pellet densities, supporting the correlation of impedance data with bulk transport.
The solubility limit of Si4+ is reached around x=0.35, beyond which phase segregation may occur.
